title: N+1 Queries and Pool Budget
instructions: Implement `QueryCounter`, `load_naive`, `load_batched`, `Budget`, `connection_budget` and `largest_pool_size` in `nplus1.py` using only `sqlite3`. The counter records SELECT statements through a trace callback, the naive loader shows the N+1 pattern, the batched loader issues one `IN (...)` query per chunk, and the budget functions check whether a fleet's connection pools fit the database limit.

evidence.label: load_batched returns the same mapping with 2 queries, the second using IN (...)
Chunks the IN list: 1 + ceil(N / chunk_size) queries
Maps childless parents to [] and issues one query when there are no parents
Orders by id everywhere and only loads the requested user's rows
QueryCounter counts only SELECTs (any case) and stops counting after the block
QueryCounter removes its callback even when the block raises
connection_budget computes worst case, availability and fits
largest_pool_size returns the largest pool that fits, or 0
